title: Batch scheduler oddity log - midnight triage
body:
Context: noticed a p99 latency bump on the late-night small-batch workload (mixed short/long queries). This doc is a fast scratchpad for reproductions, hypotheses, commands, and next steps. Notes are messy — for my own memory.

Summary:
- Time window: ~2024-08-21 01:15-02:00 UTC.
- Symptom: p99 generation latency doubled for 512-token avg requests; throughput steady.
- Surface-level: scheduler seemed to favor grouping a long request (~>2s) into early batch cycles with short requests, causing head-of-line delays.
- Impact: affecting a small subset of dedicated pods (capacity group d-3).

Quick reproduction steps I ran: (local-ish)
1) use loadgen profile: mix_a = 80% short (<=40 tokens), 20% long (>=1024 tokens), rps=45
2) run: tools/loadgen --profile mix_a --target-pool d-3 --duration 10m
3) capture traces: http://tracing.internal/svc/runtime?trace=last

Immediate observations:
- CPU/GPU utilization unchanged; kernel runtime stalls coincide with a scheduling decision logged as "batch_opened: id=xxx, expected_wait=12ms" then "batch_dispatched_with_long_token".
- KV cache hit-rate stable; not the culprit.
- Batching window metric (batch_wait_ms) occasionally spiked to 40-80ms when combining long+short sequences.
- Per-request meta: short requests that ended up in the same batch as a long request saw token-generation tail-latency multiples (p99 ~2.1s).

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Scheduler fairness bug: when a long request is queued, the scheduler doesn't split or prioritize short requests into separate batches fast enough (race in the wake-up path).
2) Batching gating uses a naive max_duration that doesn't adapt to estimated remaining tokens for in-flight items.
3) A memory fence or lock in the kernel path causes short stalls when a large KV flush happens for long runs.
4) Edge: network hiccup delaying a small set of RPCs that then get co-batched. (low probability given trace)

Quick test ideas:
- A: tweak scheduler to prefer short-only batches for high short_ratio workloads (local flag: SCHED_PREFER_SHORT=1) and compare.
- B: enable experimental per-request expected_tokens metadata and observe if scheduler avoids mixing. (branch: pr/2345 has hooks)
- C: add an exponential backoff on batch_wait_ms when a long request is detected to let short items go ahead (cheap hack).

Commands I ran (notes):
- docker exec -it runtime-dev ./bin/loadgen --profile mix_a --rps 45 --pool d-3 --out /tmp/lg-mixA.json
- curl -s "http://metrics.local/api/series?metric=batch_wait_ms&from=2024-08-21T00:55&to=2024-08-21T02:05" | jq '.' > batch_wait_21.json
- grep -n "batch_dispatched_with_long_token" runtime-logs-2024-08-21.log | head -n 30 > long_dispatch_samples.txt

Quick diffs I want to try tomorrow:
- Apply pr/2345 locally and run 30m load to measure p50/p95/p99. (expectation: p99 drop back towards baseline if scheduler chooses separate batches).
- Instrument: log estimated_remaining_tokens for each queued item and record batch composition in a compact metric.

Observed numbers (sanity):
- baseline p99 for short-only workload: ~450ms
- mixed workload p99 during incident: ~2.1s
- batch_wait_ms baseline median: 8ms, incident tail: 72ms
- GPU queue length not expanded; suggests scheduling, not kernel compute.

Notes to self / gotchas:
- When testing, ensure not to conflate KV cache misses (they spike for cold-starts) — I saw two cold-starts earlier; filter those traces.
- Need to correlate node-level GC logs (java-ish infra) — sometimes OS-level reclaiming bumps scheduling.
- Watch for autoscaler bouncing pods during the 01:10-01:20 window (saw one pod restart). Pod restarts => transient capacity skew.

Next steps (short):
- [ ] Run controlled ablation: flip SCHED_PREFER_SHORT and measure 1h run (assign: me).
- [ ] Add lightweight batch composition metric (assign: Rui).
- [ ] Post quick note to #scheduler-night with sample traces and ask if anyone changed autoscaler rules overnight (assign: Isha).

Longer-term ideas:
- Per-pool adaptive batching policy: automatically detect short-heavy mix and special-case micro-batches for short latency SLAs.
- Use request-level estimated_tokens and cost model in the scheduler to avoid mixing expensive/cheap jobs.
- Consider preemption: let short requests preempt long requests within a soft time budget.

Meeting snippet to add to tomorrow's morning huddle:
- 5 min: show trace of co-batched long+short causing p99 spike.
- 5 min: show quick A/B of SCHED_PREFER_SHORT toggle if available.
- Ask: do we want per-pool tuning or global heuristic?

Random stray notes (copied from trace):
- trace id: 8f3a2c: queue_time=13ms batch_wait=78ms dispatch_delay=62ms
- suspicious log pattern: "wake_batcher: saw_long_request but no fast-path split" appears 6x in 10m window.

If I get time tonight: try quick drop-in patch that detects any queued long request and sets batch_max_wait=8ms for next 200ms so short ones flush. Low-risk, revertable.

End of dump.
